headline: Pearl Kendrick, Grace Eldering, and the Pertussis Vaccine
blurb: In 1932, Pearl Kendrick and Grace Eldering began whooping cough research at the Michigan Department of Health laboratory in Grand Rapids, and their 1934 to 1935 field trial of a vaccine involved 1,592 children.

headline: Epidemiology of Poliomyelitis in Detroit in 1939
source: American Journal of Public Health and the Nation's Health (via PubMed Central)
blurb: A public health journal published an article in August 1941 on the spread of polio in Detroit in 1939.

headline: Detroit Diphtheria Experience of 1956
source: American Journal of Public Health and the Nation's Health (via PubMed Central)
blurb: A public health journal ran a two-page editorial in June 1957 about Detroit's experience with diphtheria in 1956.

headline: Imported Measles with Subsequent Airborne Transmission in a Pediatrician's Office -- Michigan
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Seven measles cases were reported in Muskegon County in late 1982 after a 7-month-old baby with measles arrived from Korea and four other children were infected in a pediatrician's office.

headline: Hepatitis A Associated with Consumption of Frozen Strawberries -- Michigan, March 1997
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: In March 1997, 153 hepatitis A cases were reported in Calhoun County, 151 of them in students or staff of schools in four districts, and early findings tied the illness to food items with frozen strawberries.

headline: Preliminary data shows a statewide decrease in school-age vaccine waiver rates
source: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (archived by the Internet Archive)
blurb: A Michigan rule that took effect in January 2015 requires parents who want a non-medical vaccine waiver for school to meet with local health department staff first, and a year later the state reported a 39% decrease in waivers submitted.

headline: MDHHS activates Community Health Emergency Coordination Center in response to hepatitis A outbreak
source: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (archived by the Internet Archive)
blurb: Michigan's health department opened its Community Health Emergency Coordination Center to coordinate the work of the local agencies responding to a hepatitis A outbreak.

headline: Measles cases reach 34 in Michigan, highest number since 1991 Four additional cases confirmed in Oakland County
source: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (archived by the Internet Archive)
blurb: Michigan confirmed 34 measles cases for the year, 33 of them in Oakland County, the highest number in the state since 1991, when 65 cases were reported.
